research_rationale:
Executive Order 11155 of May 23, 1964 (29 FR 6909; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11155.txt, read in full) establishes the Commission on Presidential Scholars (section 1), has the Commission choose Presidential Scholars annually under the standards in section 2 (graduating secondary school students chosen for outstanding scholarship, one boy and one girl from each State, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico and a group of territories, plus up to fifteen at large), establishes the Presidential Scholars Medallion (section 3), and has the Office of Education facilitate the order (section 4). The text states no date, duration, condition or expiry. Later instruments, each read in its held official text: Executive Order 12158 (September 18, 1979) added paragraph (5) to section 2 (up to twenty further scholars chosen for outstanding scholarship and demonstrated ability in the visual and performing arts or creative writing), and Executive Order 13697 (80 FR 36691, June 22, 2015) added paragraph (6) to section 2 (up to twenty further scholars for career and technical education); both are recorded as later events on section 2. The Office of the Federal Register note lists these two amendments and no revocation. The U.S. Code prints the order as amended (20 U.S.C. 1221 note). Some words of the original name entities that have since changed or ended (the Department of Health, Education, and Welfare and its Office of Education, the Canal Zone and the Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands); no held source shows that these changes ended any command, so every clause is treated as continuing and the changed names are disclosed rather than resolved. All twelve clauses are operative on 2026-10-14. Page check: the original is held as a machine text layer of the official Federal Register issue with location confidence medium; the check of pages 3 and 4 was made on the text layer (page markers, the running head 6910 on the second page, the heading naming the order, the signature of May 23, 1964 and the filing stamp), not on page images, which are not held. Standing note on sources: check the Federal Register pages before relying on quotations.
